Match the thermodynamics processes given under column I with expression given under column II

Column I
(A) Freezing water at 273 K and 1 atm
(B) Expansion of 1 mol of an ideal gas into a vacuum under isolated conditions.
(C) Mixing of equal volumes of two ideal gases at constant temperature and pressure in an isolated container.
(D) Reversible heating of H2(g) at 1 atm from 300K to 600K, followed by reversible cooling to 300K at 1 atm

Column II
(p) q = 0
(q) w = 0
(r) < 0
(s) = 0

i.e.; w < 0 (expansion)

Entropy of system is decreased, Ssys < 0.

U = q + w

As q < 0, w < 0 so, U < 0.

At equilibrium, G = 0.

(B) (P, Q and S)

Expansion of 1 mol of an ideal gas into a vacuum under isolated conditions,

w = 0, q = 0 so, U = 0

For expansion, Ssys > 0 as entropy increases.

For expansion, V2 > V1

G = ve i.e.; G < 0.

(C) (P, Q and S)

Mixing of equal volumes of two ideal gases at constant temperature and pressure in an isolated container.

q = 0 (isolated)

w = PV

w = 0 ( V = 0)

Ssys > 0 (mixing of gases)

U = q + w = 0

G = H TS

G = qp TS (at constant P, T)

G = 0 TS = TS

G < 0 ( Ssys > 0)

(D) (P, Q, S and T)

Internal energy (U), entropy (S) and free energy (G) are state functions which depend only upon the state of the system and do not depend upon the path by which the state is attained.

Thus, U = 0, S = 0 and G = 0

Work and heat are path functions but the same path is retraced so, q = 0 and w = 0.

en.content: The total number of stereoisomers that can exist for M is ___________.
en.explanation:
The total number of stereo isomers = 2n = 22 = 4, where n is the number of chiral centres.

However, in bridge/bicycle compounds, the number of stereo-isomers is equal to the number of chiral centres because no carbon centres rotation is possible. Therefore, two stereoisomers would be possible for the given compound.
